qs.q: Polycystic ovarian disease is characterised by which combination of biochemical abnormalities?
o: High follicle-stimulating hormone, normal luteinizing hormone, and high oestrogen
High luteinizing hormone, low follicle-stimulating hormone, and excess androgens
Low androgens, high progesterone, and low luteinizing hormone
Low luteinizing hormone, high follicle-stimulating hormone, and low androgens
qs.e: PCOS is characterised by excess androgen production, elevated LH, and low FSH. The absence of corpora lutea on histology reflects the failure of ovulation.

ai.subject: Obstetrics & gynaecology
ai.summary: Polycystic Ovarian Disease is a hormonal disorder with excess androgens and many small ovarian cysts, causing irregular periods, infertility and metabolic issues.

sections.p: PCOS is diagnosed when a woman has at least two of the following: oligo/anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, after excluding other causes.
b: Oligo/anovulation: >35 days cycle or absent periods

sections.p: Severity is graded by the Rotterdam criteria and the NIH 2003 definition. Staging considers metabolic risk and reproductive outcome.
b: Class I: all three features present

sections.p: Primary cause is insulin resistance leading to hyperinsulinemia, which stimulates ovarian androgen production and follicular arrest.
b: Comorbid infections: HIV, hepatitis B may worsen insulin resistance

sections.p: Common symptoms include irregular periods, hirsutism, acne, weight gain, and infertility. Some women are asymptomatic and found on routine ultrasound.
Tests confirm diagnosis, assess severity, and rule out mimickers.

t.b: A high ratio suggests PCOS but is not diagnostic alone.

t.a: Screen for thyroid, prolactin, and CA‑125
t.b: Excludes other endocrine or ovarian pathologies.

sections.p: Complications can be metabolic, reproductive or psychiatric. Red flags require urgent care.
Treat underlying insulin resistance, control symptoms, and monitor for complications.
b: Regular monitoring: glucose, lipids, liver function

sections.p: Regular check‑ups assess metabolic health and reproductive goals. Prevention focuses on early lifestyle changes.
Some tests may give false negatives or positives.
b: Ultrasound may miss polycystic ovaries in obese patients due to poor acoustic windows

whenToSeekHelp: Signs of diabetes or cardiovascular crisis

faq.q: Is weight loss enough to treat PCOS?
faq.a: Weight loss helps but often requires medication for hormonal balance.
